overview: Two photosynthetic pathways differing in the first stable carbon product formed and how well they handle heat and dry conditions.
genZNote: C3 plants: the classic, straightforward route. C4 plants: the upgraded version built for hot, dry climates.

aspects.label: First Stable Product of CO2 Fixation
Primary CO2-Fixing Enzyme
aspects.valueB: PEP carboxylase (initially), then RuBisCO in bundle sheath cells.

aspects.label: Leaf Anatomy
aspects.valueA: Normal leaf anatomy without distinct bundle sheath chloroplasts.
aspects.valueB: Kranz anatomy — a distinct ring of bundle sheath cells with chloroplasts around the vein.

aspects.label: Photorespiration
aspects.valueA: Significant photorespiration occurs, especially in hot/dry conditions, reducing efficiency.
aspects.valueB: Minimal photorespiration, due to the CO2-concentrating mechanism.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: C4 plants are more efficient in hot, sunny, dry climates because they minimise the wasteful process of photorespiration.
overlay.memoryTrick: C3 = 3-carbon first product. C4 = 4-carbon first product, built with Kranz anatomy for hot climates.
overlay.commonMisconception: C4 plants are not simply 'better' than C3 plants in all conditions — they only outperform C3 plants specifically under high light, heat, and low water conditions.
